(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | highlights = * [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]] winner ([[2024–25 Greek Basketball Cup|2025]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2016) }} '''Wenyen Makuac Gabriel''' (born March 26, 1997) is a South Sudanese-American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], after being a 5-star prospect in 2016, ranked as high as #14 on ESPN's Top 100. Gabriel has also played in the [[NBA]] for the [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. ==High school career== [[File:2016 Jordan Brand Classic (26255716570).jpg|thumb|left|Gabriel (32) at the 2016 Jordan Brand Classic]] Gabriel attended [[Wilbraham & Monson Academy]] in [[Wilbraham, Massachusetts|Wilbraham]], [[Massachusetts]] beginning in 2014.{{Cite web|title = Wenyen Gabriel's High School Basketball Stats|url = http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/wenyen-gabriel/2dl51g3jEeS00gAmVebEWg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm|website = MaxPreps.com|access-date = February 12, 2016}} Prior to that, he played at [[Trinity High School (Manchester, New Hampshire)|Trinity High School]] in [[Manchester, New Hampshire|Manchester]], [[New Hampshire]] for three years.{{Cite web|title = Ex-Trinity hoop star Wenyen Gabriel commits to Kentucky|url = http://www.unionleader.com/Ex-Trinity-hoop-star-Wenyen-Gabriel-commits-to-Kentucky|website = UnionLeader.com|access-date = February 12, 2016|archive-date = February 15, 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160215094226/http://www.unionleader.com/Ex-Trinity-hoop-star-Wenyen-Gabriel-commits-to-Kentucky|url-status = dead}} As a senior in 2015–16, he averaged 22.0 [[points per game]], 14.0 [[rebounds per game]], 7.0 blocks per game and 6.3 assists per game. In October 2015, he announced his decision to enroll at the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]]. [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Connecticut Huskies|UConn]] and [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] were other schools on his shortlist.{{Cite web|title = Kentucky basketball: Wenyen Gabriel commits to Wildcats, coach John Calipari|url = http://www.upi.com/Sports_News/College-Basketball/2015/10/02/Kentucky-basketball-Wenyen-Gabriel-committs-to-Wildcats-coach-John-Calipari/9551443805242/|website = UPI|access-date = February 12, 2016}} He played 19:17 minutes in the 2016 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], scoring two points, grabbing four rebounds and dishing out two assists.{{Cite web|url = http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/04/usa-wins-2016-nike-hoop-summit.aspx|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160411171636/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/04/usa-wins-2016-nike-hoop-summit.aspx|url-status = dead|archive-date = April 11, 2016|title = USA Wins Nike Hoop Summit 101-67|website = www.usab.com|access-date = April 10, 2016}} He also played in the 2016 [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. Gabriel was rated as a five-star recruit and ranked #14 in the Class of 2016 by [[ESPN]]. ==College career== He made his debut for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] in an exhibition game on October 31, 2016, against [[Clarion University of Pennsylvania|Clarion University]], tallying nine points, two rebounds and one assist in 17 minutes coming off the bench.{{Cite news|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/game-center/57334e14e4b0478276891c4e/|title=Live Basketball (M)! Clarion vs. Kentucky|newspaper=University of Kentucky - Official Athletics Site|access-date=November 12, 2016|archive-date=November 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113033704/http://www.ukathletics.com/game-center/57334e14e4b0478276891c4e/|url-status=dead}} As a freshman, he played in 38 games, including 23 starts, averaging 4.6 points and 4.8 rebounds in 17.8 minutes.{{Cite news|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/page/team-stats_m-baskbl_stat-crew|title=Basketball (M) Stats - UK Wildcats|work=University of Kentucky - Official Athletics Site|access-date=April 18, 2017}} During his sophomore year, Gabriel became more of a key figure for Kentucky's success that season, tallying 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds in 37 games. He led Kentucky with 40 blocked shots.{{Cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4122|title=Wenyen Gabriel - 2017-18 Men's Basketball Roster - University of Kentucky|website=ukathletics.com|date=August 10, 2017 |access-date=June 23, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2018–2020)=== Gabriel declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]],{{cite news|title=Forty-three international early entry candidates withdraw from NBA Draft 2018|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/12/forty-three-international-early-entry-candidates-withdraw-nba-draft-2018|work=NBA.com|date=June 12, 2018|access-date=June 23, 2018}} but went undrafted.{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Fisher|title=NBA Draft 2018: Kentucky's Wenyen Gabriel goes undrafted|url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/NBA-Draft-2018-Kentuckys-Wenyen-Gabriel-goes-undrafted-119263791/|work=CatsPause|date=June 22, 2018|access-date=June 23, 2018}} He joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Jack|last=Pilgrim|title=Official: Wenyen Gabriel joins Sacramento Kings for Summer League|url=https://kentuckysportsradio.com/nba-cats/official-wenyen-gabriel-joins-sacramento-kings-for-summer-league/|website=KentuckySportsRadio.com|access-date=June 25, 2018}} On July 31, 2018, he signed a two-way contract with the Kings.{{cite news|title=Kings Sign Wenyen Gabriel to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-wenyen-gabriel-to-two-way-contract|work=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2018|access-date=August 2, 2018}} However, he did not appear in a game during that season. Just prior to the start of the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]], the Kings converted Gabriel's contract to a standard deal.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Roster Moves Wenyen Gabriel Elevated to Roster Spot, DaQuan Jeffries Added as Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-announce-roster-moves|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2019|access-date=October 21, 2019}} He had a double-double of 16 points and 16 rebounds for the [[Stockton Kings]] on December 20, 2019, in a win over the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite news|title=Kings' Wenyen Gabriel: Collects double-double Thursday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-wenyen-gabriel-collects-double-double-thursday/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=December 20, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2020}} On January 11, 2020, Gabriel had 37 points, 11 rebounds and three assists for Stockton in its 163–143 win over the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite news|title=Kings' Wenyen Gabriel: Returns from G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-wenyen-gabriel-returns-from-g-league/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 12, 2020|access-date=January 13, 2020}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2020)=== On January 20, 2020, Gabriel was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] along with [[Trevor Ariza]] and [[Caleb Swanigan]] in exchange for [[Kent Bazemore]], [[Anthony Tolliver]] and two future second round picks.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Trevor Ariza, Wenyen Gabriel, and Caleb Swanigan from Sacramento|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/1/20/trail-blazers-acquire-trevor-ariza-wenyen-gabriel-caleb-swanigan-from-sacramento|website=NBA.com|date=January 20, 2020|access-date=January 21, 2020}} He made his debut for the Trail Blazers on January 31, going 0-for-3 from the field with one rebound, one assist and a block in 13 minutes as the Blazers defeated the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] 127–119.{{cite web|first=John|last=Aubin|title=Wenyen Gabriel starts game for Blazers on Friday|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/249461/wenyen-gabriel-starts-game-blazers-on-friday.php|website=Fantasy Pros|date=February 1, 2020|access-date=February 1, 2020}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2020–2021)=== On November 30, 2020, Gabriel signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Wenyen Gabriel and Willy Hernangómez|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-weynen-gabriel-and-willy-hernangomez|website=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2020|access-date=December 2, 2020}} In 21 games with the team he averaged 11.5 minutes, 3.5 points, 2.69 rebounds, and 0.4 blocks per game. He was waived just prior to the start of the [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]].{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Inabinett|title=Pelicans adding third Alabama alumnus to training-camp roster|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2021/10/pelicans-adding-third-alabama-alumnus-to-training-camp-roster.html|work=[[Al.com]]|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2021}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2021)=== In October 2021, Gabriel joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2021 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2021-training-camp-roster/n-5758540|website=OurSports Central.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}} In 12 games he averaged 13.8 points on 47.5 percent shooting from the field and 38.7 percent shooting from 3-point range, 8.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.0 blocks in 25.8 minutes per contest.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Wenyen Gabriel to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/12/21/brooklyn-nets-sign-wenyen-gabriel-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2021)=== On December 21, 2021, Gabriel signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. He played one game for the team. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2021–2022)=== On December 31, 2021, Gabriel signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite news |title=Clippers' Wenyen Gabriel: To sign with Clippers |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-wenyen-gabriel-to-sign-with-clippers/ |access-date=December 31, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 31, 2021}} He signed a third 10-day contract with the Clippers on January 11, 2022.{{cite news |title=Clippers' Wenyen Gabriel: Re-ups with Clippers |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-wenyen-gabriel-re-ups-with-clippers/ |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 11, 2022}} ===Second stint with Wisconsin (2022)=== Following the expiration of his second 10-day contract, Gabriel was re-acquired by the [[Wisconsin Herd]] on January 21.{{cite web | url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/ | title=NBA G League Transactions }} On January 29, 2022, Gabriel signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web|title=Pelicans sign Wenyen Gabriel to 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-wenyen-gabriel-10-day-contract-1-29-22|access-date=January 29, 2022|website=NBA}} He did not play in a game for the Pelicans before his deal expired. On February 8, he was reacquired by the Herd.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 8, 2022|access-date=February 8, 2022}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2022–2023)=== [[File:Wenyen Gabriel (March 21, 2022) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Gabriel with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2022]] On March 1, 2022, Gabriel signed a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign D.J. Augustin and Wenyen Gabriel|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-dj-augustin-wenyen-gabriel-3-1-22|website=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2022|access-date=March 1, 2022}} On April 8, 2022, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] converted Gabriel's [[two-way contract]] into a two-year standard contract.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Wenyen Gabriel To Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-wenyen-gabriel-standard-nba-contract-4-8-22|website=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2022|access-date=April 8, 2022}} With the Lakers, in 68 games in which he played 15.1 minutes per game, he averaged 5.5 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 0.5 blocks per game, with a .596 field goal percentage. On October 3, 2023, Gabriel signed with the [[Boston Celtics]],{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Sign Gabriel|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease-20230311boston-celtics-sign-gabriel|website=NBA.com|date=October 3, 2023|access-date=October 3, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Celtics Waive Wenyen Gabriel, DJ Steward|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/celtics-to-waive-wenyen-gabriel.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}} ===Third stint with Wisconsin / Memphis Grizzlies (2023–2024)=== On October 30, 2023, Gabriel joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]]{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd Announce 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 23, 2024}} and on March 8, 2024, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Wenyen Gabriel to 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-wenyen-gabriel-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2024|access-date=March 8, 2024}} With Memphis, in five games he averaged 16.2 minutes, 3.4 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 0.4 blocks per game. On March 18, he returned to Wisconsin.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Wisconsin Herd Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Wisconsin-Herd/50/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 18, 2024}} ===Vaqueros de Bayamón (2024)=== On March 11, 2024, Gabriel signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]].{{cite web|title=Los Vaqueros anuncian la firma del sudanés Wenyen Gabriel como su primer refuerzo|url=https://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/los-vaqueros-anuncia-la-firma-del-sudanes-wenyen-gabriel-como-su-primer-refuerzo/|website=PrimeraHora.com|date=March 11, 2024|access-date=March 18, 2024|language=Spanish}} In 23 games he averaged 13.0 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks (7th in the league) per game, with a .576 field goal percentage.[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Wenyen-Gabriel/Summary/88737 "Wenyen Gabriel,"] basketball.realgm.com. === Maccabi Tel Aviv (2024) === On July 10, 2024, Gabriel signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague|Euroleague]].{{cite web |title=מכבי החתימה את ווניין גבריאל |url=https://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=16276 |access-date=11 September 2024 |date=10 July 2024}} During September he suffered an injury that left him out for 3–4 weeks.{{Cite web |title=Πλήγμα με Γκέιμπριελ στην Μακάμπι, τέθηκε εκτός για 3-4 εβδομάδες |url=https://www.sport24.gr/basket/makampi-pligma-me-gkeimpriel-tethike-ektos-gia-3-4-evdomades.10383005.html |access-date=2024-09-23 |website=www.sport24.gr |date=September 23, 2024 |language=el}} === Panathinaikos (2024–2025) === Wenyen Gabriel signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] and the [[EuroLeague]] on December 23, 2024, to fill the gap left by Mathias Lessort until the end of the season.{{Cite web |date=2024-12-23 |title=Wenyen Gabriel is set for midseason move to Panathinaikos |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1761961/wenyen-gabriel-set-to-sign-with-panathinaikos-euroleague/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} During his time with the team, Gabriel made an immediate impact, averaging 6.0 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 0.9 blocks per game in the EuroLeague, and posting a career-high 16 points against [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena Zvezda]] on April 11, 2025.{{Cite web |title=Wenyen Gabriel EuroLeague Stats |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/players/wenyen-gabriel/013383/ |website=EuroLeague |access-date=2025-08-20}} His energetic playing style, defensive presence, and versatility quickly endeared him to Panathinaikos fans, who appreciated his hustle and commitment on the court.{{Cite web |title=Wenyen Gabriel admired by Panathinaikos fans |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1845731/wenyen-gabriel-signs-with-bayern-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |date=July 7, 2025 |access-date=2025-08-20}} At the end of the season, Gabriel left the team due to restrictions on the number of foreign players in the Greek Basketball League, with his roster spot being given to veteran NBA center [[Richaun Holmes]].{{Cite web |title=Wenyen Gabriel signs with Bayern after Panathinaikos |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1845731/wenyen-gabriel-signs-with-bayern-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |date=July 7, 2025 |access-date=2025-08-20}} === Bayern Munich (2025–2026) === On June 28, 2025, Gabriel signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] and [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=EuroLeague rookie center moves from Greece to Germany|url=https://basketnews.com/news-227296-wenyen-gabriel-leaves-panathinaikos-joins-bayern.html|access-date=July 5, 2025|website=basketnews.com|language=en}} === Beşiktaş (2026–present) === On July 31, 2026, Gabriel signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Beşiktaş sign Wenyen Gabriel|url=https://bjk.com.tr/en/news/94821/besiktas-sign-wenyen-gabriel.html|date=August 1, 2026|access-date=August 2, 2026|website=bjk.com.tr|language=en}} ==National team career== Gabriel joined the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan national team]] in August 2023, as he was selected in the roster for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], where South Sudan made their international debut.{{Cite web |title=Lakers forward Wenyen Gabriel fortifies South Sudan World Cup squad |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/lakers-forward-wenyen-gabriel-fortifies-south-sudan-world-cup-squad |access-date=2023-08-11 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=August 8, 2023 |language=en}} Gabriel and the South Sudanese team made history for the nation by placing first out of all African nations at the tournament. The team was granted automatic qualification for the [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Paris Olympics]] men's basketball tournament,{{Cite news |author=Deng Machol|agency=Associated Press |date=2023-09-09 |title='The world knows us.' Two weeks after he was born, Gabriel's mother, Rebecca Gak, moved with him and his three siblings to [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]] to escape the violence of the [[Second Sudanese Civil War]]. While Gabriel's mother worked to earn enough money to move his father, Makuac, to Cairo, his seven-year-old brother, Komot, became Gabriel's primary care giver.{{Cite web|title = Wenyen Gabriel: From Africa war to doorstep of NCAA hoops elites|url = https://nypost.com/2015/08/21/wenyen-gabriel-from-africa-war-to-doorstep-of-ncaa-hoops-elites/|website = New York Post|access-date = February 12, 2016|first = Zach|last = Braziller| date=August 22, 2015 }} Two years after moving to Egypt, the [[United Nations]] granted an appeal to move the refugee family to [[Manchester, New Hampshire]], an American city with a large South Sudanese population. Gabriel became a US citizen in 2017 when his parents became citizens. He received his paperwork and passport in 2015,{{Cite web|url=http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/high_school/high_school_insider/2015/12/prep_school_baskeball_wilbraham_monson_standout|title=Prep School {{sic|Baske|ball|hide=y}}: Wilbraham & Monson standout Wenyen Gabriel selected to the USA Basketball Juniors National Team|website=www.bostonherald.com|access-date=June 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318185819/http://www.bostonherald.com/news/local_coverage/2018/03/deadly_fire_kills_3_injures_7_displaces_dozens_more|archive-date=March 18, 2018}} and represented the [[USA Basketball Junior National Select Team]] at the 2016 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. In 2016, he said he still considers [[South Sudan]] his home.{{Cite web|title = USA Selection Caps Rise For Wenyen Gabriel|date=February 8, 2016|publisher=USA Basketball|url = http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/02/usa-selection-for-wenyen-gabriel.aspx|access-date = February 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160212023728/http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/02/usa-selection-for-wenyen-gabriel.aspx|archive-date=February 12, 2016}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{basketballstats |nba=1629117 |bbr=g/gabriwe01}} * {{Official website|https://wenyengabriel.com}} * [https://ukathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4122 Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{Beşiktaş J.K.
